newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine hopes for $1.5 bln IMF currency fund soon.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine hopes for $1.5 bln IMF currency fund soon.

text.p: Ukraine expects to soon receive a $1.5 billion currency stabilisation fund from the International Monetary Fund for its new hryvna currency, a presidential adviser said on Wednesday.
Volodymyr Kuznetsov, the president's adviser on investment matters, told a news conference that conditions were favourable for introducing the hryvna on September 2.
"The National Bank has the currency market under control and there are hopes that we will soon receive a stabilisation fund from the IMF," he said.
IMF officials have previously said that a stabilisation fund was still under discussion. The IMF and Ukraine failed to settle it in talks last week.
Kuznetsov said the main purpose of the stabilisation fund would be psychological.

"The central bank has plenty of resources, enough to maintain the current rate for the foreseeable future," said Kuznetsov, also the new head of Ukraine's investment promotion body, the Ukrainian National Credit-Investment Company.
The current interim karbovanets currency will be phased out by September 16. The hryvna will be worth 100,000 karbovanets.
